name: build-toolchain-pins
body: Build toolchains are pinned so a release is reproducible, exactly where the toolchain mechanism or the closest build path can enforce it. Rust is exact wherever rustup resolves it: a root `rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel = 1.98.1`) is found by rustup's parent-walk from the apg crate and all three cargo frontend crates, and CI uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.98.1`; the Homebrew `bottle` path uses Homebrew's unversioned `rust`, which is not rustup and so ignores the file. Node is enforced fail-closed on the 26.x line, not an exact patch: `src/tslib/.npmrc` sets `engine-strict=true` and `src/tslib/package.json`'s `engines.node` is the range `>=26.8.1 <27` (Homebrew's `node` floats within the line, so an exact patch would fail against a patch it has not shipped), while CI uses `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: '26.9.0'`. Go is exact on the release Linux path but a documented floor elsewhere: the `linux` job sets `GOTOOLCHAIN: 'go1.27.1'` with `actions/setup-go@v5 go-version: '1.27.1'`, while `src/golib/go.mod` carries `toolchain go1.27.1` as the repo-visible floor — the `bottle` job builds through the split Homebrew formulae whose `depends_on 'go'` is unversioned. JDK 21 (`actions/setup-java`) and .NET 10.0.x (`actions/setup-dotnet`) are pinned in CI. The pin consumers are the paths that actually build: the CI `linux` job (`cargo build --release`, which drives `build.rs`) and `bottle` job (via the split formulae), plus those formulae themselves; `install.sh` is download-only — it fetches prebuilt release tarballs and never builds a frontend — so it consumes no toolchain and is not a pin consumer. Acceptance: `release.yml` names the exact Rust pin (the action ref), the exact Node CI version and the Go release pin; Node's `engine-strict` admits the whole 26.x line; and the Homebrew rust/node behaviour and the Go floor are documented for the bottle/ambient path.
